crossStoryFindings: Stories 1-7 are wired end to end through shared archive contracts, Convex archive tables, Fastify archive routes, execution finalization hooks, and the client archive/turn/derived-view surfaces.
Archive-entry degradation now propagates consistently into turn and derived-view rebuilds via shared enrichment, so detached or missing provenance no longer degrades only the archive page.
Long-history behavior diverges across surfaces: archive entries and turns expose bounded paging, but derived views truncate after 50 items with no continuation signal.
architectureFindings: The canonical separation is intact: live websocket/current-object history remains on the process work surface, while finalized archive writes flow through `ArchiveFinalizationService` into `archiveEntries`.

Derived-view reads drift from the tech design's cursor-bounded read contract. The design calls for cursor pagination with a default derived-view limit, but the current API exposes no paging inputs and silently slices the computed set.
The default production execution stack uses real Local and Daytona adapters, but the script layer is still one shared runtime-audit payload rather than process-type-specific execution logic.
epicCoverageAssessment: Both requested gates passed: `corepack pnpm run green-verify` and `corepack pnpm run verify-all`.

Automated happy-path coverage is strong across Convex, server, client, and integration tests for archive persistence, finalization, read/reopen, turn derivation, derived views, and provenance degradation.

Gate coverage still has explicit gaps: `guard:no-test-changes` and `test:e2e` are scaffold-only `SKIP` scripts, so there is still no executable browser/runtime end-to-end archive scenario enforced by automation.
productionPathFindings: No fake provider adapter is wired into the default production registry: `DefaultProviderAdapterRegistry` resolves real Local and Daytona adapters, while `SingleAdapterRegistry` and `InMemoryProviderAdapter` stay test-only.

The remaining non-real execution-path concern is the shared `buildIntegratedRuntimeAuditPayload` path, which generates a generic workspace-inspection run for every execution instead of process-type-specific runtime logic.
No fake archive store or shim route was found in the archive read/write path itself; archive persistence still flows through Fastify services and `PlatformStore` into Convex.

nonBlockingFindings.title: Derived archive views are hard-capped at 50 with no pagination contract
nonBlockingFindings.evidence: Flow 7 says archive entries, turns, and derived views use cursor pagination with default limits, including derived views at a default of 50 (`docs/spec-build/v2/epics/07--archive-and-derived-views/tech-design.md:668-674`). The derived-view route exposes no paging query (`apps/platform/server/schemas/archive.ts:37-44`), the shared response has no page metadata (`apps/platform/shared/contracts/archive.ts:282-285`), and the service simply `slice(0, 50)`s computed views (`apps/platform/server/services/archive/derived-archive-view.service.ts:210-211`). Once a process has more than 33 turns, some `turn_range`/`chunk_candidate` views become unreachable with no `hasMore` signal.

nonBlockingFindings.title: Production execution still runs through one shared runtime-audit payload
nonBlockingFindings.evidence: `createApp` constructs `new ScriptExecutionService(providerAdapterRegistry)` by default (`apps/platform/server/app.ts:285-286`). `ScriptExecutionService` then always builds `buildIntegratedRuntimeAuditPayload(...)` unless a custom factory is injected (`apps/platform/server/services/processes/environment/script-execution.service.ts:298-356`). That payload emits a generic workspace-inspection run with fixed archive/tool/model/process shapes (`apps/platform/server/services/processes/environment/script-execution.service.ts:18-295`). This is not a fake provider path, but it is still a generic execution path rather than process-type-specific runtime logic.

nonBlockingFindings.title: Story and epic gate commands still include scaffold-only checks
nonBlockingFindings.evidence: `guard:no-test-changes` only prints `SKIP: guard:no-test-changes not implemented for this repo yet` and `test:e2e` only prints `SKIP: test:e2e scaffolded in Story 0; no executable suite yet` (`package.json:23-27`). `green-verify` and `verify-all` passed, but those gate legs are not yet enforcing the intended protections.

unresolvedItems: Decide whether the shared runtime-audit payload is an accepted interim production path or should be replaced before archive contents are treated as fully domain-real.
Decide whether derived-view reads should implement the cursor pagination promised in the tech design, or whether the spec should explicitly bless a hard 50-view cap.
Replace the scaffolded `guard:no-test-changes` and `test:e2e` scripts if those protections are required for future epic gates.

crossStoryFindings: Stories 2, 6, and 7 drift together on checkpoint-bound archive material: finalized runtime entries that need artifact/source linkage are withheld from the canonical archive until a later async checkpoint phase, so the archive can be incomplete immediately after execution completes.

Stories 4, 5, and 7 are wired end-to-end, but the turn/view surfaces behave like rebuilders instead of cached bounded readers: every GET re-derives from the full archive, and derived views stop at the first 50 records with no way to read the remainder.
architectureFindings: Tech-design Q7/Flow 6 says archive rows should store nullable related ids and stay readable even when related context is unavailable; the implementation instead defers some rows until checkpoint provenance resolves.

Tech-design Q5/Q8 says cached turns and derived views exist to keep long reads bounded, but the current read path full-scans and rewrites caches on every request and omits derived-view pagination altogether.
epicCoverageAssessment: Most Epic 7 behaviors are implemented and covered by passing automation: canonical archive taxonomy, idempotent append, authenticated archive/turn/view routes, provenance enrichment, degraded-entry rendering, and reload/reopen flows all have automated coverage.

Coverage is weak around the completion-to-checkpoint window: the orchestrator tests explicitly poll for deferred archive rows to appear later, which means the suite does not prove immediate canonical visibility for all finalized entries.
Long-process coverage proves a hard cap of 50 derived views, but it does not prove a contract for paging through the full derived-view set.
productionPathFindings: Production createApp wiring uses the real Convex store, Local/Daytona provider registry, and Octokit checkpoint writer; the in-memory stores/adapters remain test seams rather than the live execution path.

The material production-path gap is the async checkpoint bridge: some finalized archive rows are only appended after background checkpoint work finishes, so canonical archive completeness depends on a later phase instead of the completion boundary itself.

blockingFindings.title: Checkpoint-bound archive entries are not appended at finalization time
blockingFindings.evidence: `ProcessEnvironmentService.applyExecutionResultSideEffects` diverts any runtime archive entry with `artifactCheckpointIndex` or `sourceProvenanceBinding` into `deferredArchiveEntries` instead of appending it immediately (`apps/platform/server/services/processes/environment/process-environment.service.ts:731-735,1789-1790`). In the normal production path, successful execution then schedules `runCheckpointAsync` and returns without appending those rows (`apps/platform/server/services/processes/environment/process-environment.service.ts:644-662`). The actual append happens later inside checkpoint execution (`apps/platform/server/services/processes/environment/process-environment.service.ts:1024-1031,1108-1115`). The orchestration test has to poll until `script:live-archive-1` eventually appears, proving the row is not immediately durable after completion (`tests/service/server/process-execution-orchestrator.test.ts:731-749`). This leaves a crash/reload window where finalized material is missing from the canonical archive.

blockingFindings.title: Turn and derived-view reads do not implement the bounded cached-read contract
blockingFindings.evidence: `DefaultTurnDerivationService.getTurns` always calls `rebuildTurns` before serving any page (`apps/platform/server/services/archive/turn-derivation.service.ts:81-98`), and `rebuildTurns` always full-scans the archive via `listAllArchiveEntries` before rewriting the entire turn cache (`apps/platform/server/services/archive/turn-derivation.service.ts:54-69,102-124`). `DefaultDerivedArchiveViewService.listViews` likewise rebuilds turns and rewrites derived views on every GET (`apps/platform/server/services/archive/derived-archive-view.service.ts:61-74`). After rebuilding, the service hard-slices the derived-view set to 50 (`apps/platform/server/services/archive/derived-archive-view.service.ts:25,66,210-211`), while the shared contract and route schema expose no cursor or page metadata for derived views (`apps/platform/shared/contracts/archive.ts:282-289`,`apps/platform/server/schemas/archive.ts:37-46`). The client can only report how many structural views it got, with no affordance to fetch omitted results (`apps/platform/client/features/processes/derived-archive-views-section.ts:46-49`).

unresolvedItems: The first `corepack pnpm run green-verify` run failed once in `tests/service/server/process-live-updates.test.ts:1397`, but a full rerun of `green-verify` and `verify-all` passed. I could not determine whether that was a timing flake or a one-off environment hiccup.
I did not execute the manual live-service checklist with `pnpm run convex:dev` and `pnpm dev`; conclusions are based on code review plus automated gate runs.
